entities.summary: Juan Fernández de Velasco, 5th Duke of Frías was a prominent Spanish nobleman and diplomat who played a crucial role in the early modern era. Born into a prominent family in the 16th century, he ascended to the dukedom in 1579 and served as a trusted advisor to King Philip II of Spain. Throughout his life, he was involved in various diplomatic missions, including the Treaty of Antwerp (1568) and the Peace of Vervins (1590), which helped to secure peace between Spain and France. He also participated in the Spanish colonization of the Americas, particularly in the establishment of the Spanish colony of New Mexico. Fernández de Velasco's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his diplomatic efforts helped to shape the course of European politics in the 17th century. As a testament to his enduring influence, the city of Frías, Spain, still bears his name today. The 5th Duke of Frías was a key figure in the early modern era, whose diplomatic prowess and strategic thinking had a lasting impact on the continent. His name is still remembered in the annals of Spanish history, a reminder of the enduring legacy of a man who played a significant role in shaping the course of European politics.

entities.summary: Juan Fernández de Velasco, 5th Duke of Frías was a Spanish nobleman and diplomat who played a pivotal role in the royal court of King Philip III of Spain during the early modern period. He served as a trusted advisor to the king and participated in key diplomatic missions to European powers, including France and England. Through his efforts, Velasco helped shape Spain's foreign policy and contributed to the country's growing influence on the continent. His legacy can be seen in the many treaties and agreements he negotiated, which had far-reaching consequences for Spanish relations with other nations. As a member of the powerful Velasco family, Juan Fernández de Velasco was born into a world of wealth and privilege, but his own life was marked by both triumph and tragedy. He died on March 15, 1613, at the age of 63, leaving behind a complex and multifaceted legacy that continues to be studied by historians today.
